extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) and PTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing secrecy orders, permits/modify permissions, licenses for foreign filing/export of technical data, and petitions (including retroactive) relevant to patent applications made in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy order issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified by the chief officer of a defense agency that publication or disclosure of the invention by the granting of a patent would be detrimental to the national security, an order that the invention be kept secret will be issued by the Commissioner for Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy orders are issued upon notification from a defense agency that disclosure would be detrimental to national security. The issuance is by the Commissioner for Patents; follow-up procedural rules (notification, suspension, permits) apply elsewhere in the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation requests for secrecy orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for compensation as provided in 35 U.S.C. 183 must not be made to the Patent and Trademark Office, but directly to the department or agency which caused the secrecy order to be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking statutory compensation under 35 U.S.C. 183 should address the responsible department/agency rather than the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: subsequent applications disclosing significant subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: An application disclosing any significant part of the subject matter of an application under a secrecy order pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section also falls within the scope of such secrecy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any pending application that discloses significant subject matter in common with a secret application must be promptly brought to Licensing and Review (unless itself already under a secrecy order). Subsequently filed applications containing significant subject matter must be hand-carried to Licensing and Review or mailed per §5.1(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution must continue to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: National applications under secrecy order which come to a final rejection must be appealed or otherwise prosecuted to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must complete appeals/prosecution even while under secrecy order; however, appeals generally will not be set for hearing until the secrecy order is removed unless specifically ordered otherwise by the Commissioner for Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference or derivation not instituted while secret
rubrics_metrics.description: An interference or derivation will not be instituted involving a national application under secrecy order. An applicant may suggest an interference (§41.202(a)), but the Office will not act on the request while the application remains under a secrecy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to institute interference/derivation may be suggested but are not processed while the application remains secret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when application is in condition for allowance except secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: When the national application is found to be in condition for allowance except for the secrecy order the applicant and the agency which caused the secrecy order to be issued will be notified. This notice (which is not a notice of allowance under §1.311) does not require reply and places the national application in a condition of suspension until the secrecy order is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will hold the file in suspension and will issue a proper notice of allowance or take other action only after the secrecy order is removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications under secrecy order not transmitted
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications and international design applications under secrecy order will not be mailed, delivered, or otherwise transmitted to the international authorities or the applicant. International applications under secrecy order will be processed up to the point where record and search copies would be transmitted to the international authorities or the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing stops before transmission of records/search copies; do not transmit secret international filings to authorities or applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rescission — who may file and form
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for rescission or removal of a secrecy order may be filed by, or on behalf of, any principal affected thereby. Such petition may be in letter form, and it must be in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any principal affected by a secrecy order may file; file in duplicate and letter form is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rescission must recite facts and supply prior publication evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must recite any and all facts that purport to render the order ineffectual or futile. When prior publications or patents are alleged the petition must give complete data as to such publications or patents and should be accompanied by copies thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations that prior publication defeats the need for a secrecy order require complete bibliographic data and copies of the publications/patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must identify government contracts or state none
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must identify any contract between the Government and any of the principals under which the subject matter of the application or any significant part thereof was developed or to which the subject matter is otherwise related. If there is no such contract, the petition must so state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state any related Government contract or affirm absence of such contract in the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Secretary of Commerce timing after petition denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal to the Secretary of Commerce, as provided by 35 U.S.C. 181, from a secrecy order cannot be taken until after a petition for rescission of the secrecy order has been made and denied. Appeal must be taken within sixty days from the date of the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhaust the petition for rescission before appealing; file appeal within 60 days of denial. The party appealing and the agency that caused the order will be notified of hearing time/place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit (modification) required for consent to disclosure or foreign filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent to disclosure, or to the filing of an application abroad, as provided in 35 U.S.C. 182, shall be made by a 'permit' or 'modification' of the secrecy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any consent to disclose or permit foreign filing must be formalized as a permit/modification of the secrecy order (not informal agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for permit must recite reason/purpose and clearance details
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for a permit or modification must fully recite the reason or purpose for the proposed disclosure. Where any proposed disclosee is known to be cleared by a defense agency to receive classified information, adequate explanation of such clearance should be made in the petition including the name of the agency or department granting the clearance and the date and degree thereof. The petition must be filed in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the purpose and, if disclosees hold security clearances, include agency, date, and degree of clearance; file in duplicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to permit filing abroad must list countries and disclosees and vouch for them
rubrics_metrics.description: In a petition for modification of a secrecy order to permit filing abroad, all countries in which it is proposed to file must be made known, as well as all attorneys, agents and others to whom the material will be consigned prior to being lodged in the foreign patent office. The petition should include a statement vouching for the loyalty and integrity of the proposed disclosees and where their clearance status in this or the foreign country is known all details should be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full list of countries and all persons/entities to receive the material before foreign filing; include vouching statements and clearance details where known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent in one application may apply to common subject matter in others
rubrics_metrics.description: Consent to the disclosure of subject matter from one application under secrecy order may be deemed to be consent to the disclosure of common subject matter in other applications under secrecy order so long as the subject matter is not taken out of context in a manner disclosing material beyond the modification granted in the first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: consent may be treated as covering common subject matter across files, but only if context doesn't extend disclosure beyond the original modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: General permits for organizations involved in routine operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations requiring consent for disclosure of applications under secrecy order to persons or organizations in connection with repeated routine operation may petition for such consent in the form of a general permit. To be successful such petitions must ordinarily recite the security clearance status of the disclosees as sufficient for the highest classification of material that may be involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General permits possible for routine operations; successful petitions should recite that disclosees possess appropriate clearance for highest classification likely involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: License required before filing in or exporting to a foreign country (when invention made in US)
rubrics_metrics.description: A license from the Commissioner for Patents under 35 U.S.C. 184 is required before filing any application for patent ... in a foreign country or in a foreign or international intellectual property authority ... if the invention was made in the United States, and: (1) an application on the invention has been filed in the United States less than six months prior to the date on which the application is to be filed; or (2) no application on the invention has been filed in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invention made in US, foreign filing generally requires a Commissioner license unless a US application has been on file at least six months (and not under secrecy) or other exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: License authorizes export of technical data for foreign filing and WIPO online use
rubrics_metrics.description: The license ... would also authorize the export of technical data abroad for purposes related to: (1) The preparation, filing or possible filing, and prosecution of a foreign application; and (2) The use of a World Intellectual Property Organization online service for preparing an international application for filing with the United States Patent and Trademark Office acting as a Receiving Office ... without separately complying with ITAR, EAR, and DOE regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Commissioner license can subsume certain export authorization for technical data used in foreign filing and specified WIPO online services, avoiding the need for separate export approvals in those narrow circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other export regulations when no Commissioner license
rubrics_metrics.description: Where technical data ... are being exported for purposes related to the preparation, filing or possible filing and prosecution of a foreign application, without the license from the Commissioner for Patents ... the export regulations (ITAR, EAR, DOE) must be complied with unless a license is not required because a United States application was on file at the time of export for at least six months without a secrecy order under §5.2 being placed thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not have a Commissioner license, ensure compliance with ITAR (22 CFR 120–130), EAR (15 CFR 730–774), and DOE (10 CFR 810) unless the six-month US filing exception applies and no secrecy order exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy order blocks export/foreign filing except via §5.5
rubrics_metrics.description: If a secrecy order has been issued under §5.2, an application cannot be exported to, or filed in, a foreign country ... except in accordance with §5.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A secrecy order restricts any export or foreign filing unless a permit/modification per §5.5 has been obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances where no Commissioner license is required
rubrics_metrics.description: No license pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section is required: (1) If the invention was not made in the United States, or (2) If the corresponding United States application is not subject to a secrecy order under §5.2, and was filed at least six months prior to the date on which the application is filed in a foreign country, or (3) For subsequent modifications, amendments, and supplements ... if: (i) A license is not, or was not, required under paragraph (e)(2) ...; (ii) The corresponding United States application was not required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181; and (iii) Such modifications ... do not ... change the general nature of the invention ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three principal exceptions: invention made outside US; corresponding US app on file at least six months and not under secrecy; limited subsequent changes that do not alter general nature nor require inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner license can be revoked
rubrics_metrics.description: A license pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section can be revoked at any time upon written notification by the United States Patent and Trademark Office. An authorization to file a foreign application resulting from the passage of six months from the date of filing of a United States patent application may be revoked by the imposition of a secrecy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after a license is granted or after six months' automatic authorization, the PTO can revoke permission, including by imposing a secrecy order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a US application considered an automatic petition for license
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of an application in the United States Patent and Trademark Office on an invention made in the United States will be considered to include a petition for license under 35 U.S.C. 184 for the subject matter of the application. The filing receipt or other official notice will indicate if a license is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial filing triggers an automatic petition; if the automatic petition is not granted, a separate petition per §5.12(b) may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for license must include fee and delivery instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for license must include the fee set forth in §1.17(g) of this chapter, the petitioner’s address, and full instructions for delivery of the requested license when it is to be delivered to other than the petitioner. The petition should be presented in letter form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the statutory fee, complete contact/address information, and clear delivery instructions; letter form is acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when no corresponding US application must include a copy of the material
rubrics_metrics.description: If no corresponding national, international design, or international application has been filed in the United States, the petition for license under §5.12(b) must also be accompanied by a legible copy of the material upon which a license is desired. This copy will be retained as a measure of the license granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is no US file to measure scope, submit a legible copy of the material to be licensed; PTO will retain it as the measure of the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition when corresponding US application exists must identify it
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a corresponding United States application on file, a petition for license under §5.12(b) must also identify this application by application number, filing date, inventor, and title, but a copy of the material upon which the license is desired is not required. The subject matter licensed will be measured by the disclosure of the United States application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the corresponding US application exactly; the licensed subject matter is bounded by the US application's disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining multiple US applications in one petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more United States applications should not be referred to in the same petition for license unless they are to be combined in the foreign or international application, in which event the petition should so state and the identification of each United States application should be in separate paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you must refer to multiple US files, state intention to combine them in the foreign filing and identify each US app in separate paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: When foreign filing contains new matter, furnish copy or identify new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application to be filed or exported abroad contains matter not disclosed in the United States application or applications ... a copy of the application as it is to be filed or exported abroad, must be furnished with the petition. If, however, all new matter in the application to be filed or exported is readily identifiable, the new matter may be submitted in detail and the remainder by reference to the pertinent United States application or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If foreign filing adds subject matter beyond US disclosure, provide the full foreign-file copy or clearly identify all new matter in detail; otherwise reference the US application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of license — permissible acts (general category)
rubrics_metrics.description: This license permits subsequent modifications, amendments, and supplements containing additional subject matter to, or divisions of, a foreign application, if such changes to the application do not alter the general nature of the invention in a manner that would require the United States application to have been made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181. Grant of this license authorizes the export of technical data pursuant to §5.11(b) and the filing of an application in a foreign country ... when the technical data and the subject matter of the foreign application correspond to that of the application or other materials reviewed pursuant to §§5.12 through 5.14, upon which the license was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A license may authorize amendments/divisions and export/filing provided these do not change the general nature of the invention so as to trigger inspection requirements under 35 U.S.C. 181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of license — authority to export/file duplicates and formal papers
rubrics_metrics.description: To export and file all duplicate and formal application papers in foreign countries or with foreign or international intellectual property authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License may explicitly allow export and filing of duplicate/formal application papers abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of license — authority to make amendments, modifications, supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: To make amendments, modifications, and supplements, including divisions, changes or supporting matter consisting of the illustration, exemplification, comparison, or explanation of subject matter disclosed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License can allow adding supporting materials or formal amendments that do not change the general nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of license — authority to take actions in prosecution (subject to limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: To take any action in the prosecution of the foreign application provided that the adding of subject matter or taking of any action ... does not change the general nature of the invention disclosed in the application in a manner that would require such application to have been made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181 by including technical data pertaining to: (i) Defense services or articles designated in the United States Munitions List ...; or (ii) Restricted Data, sensitive nuclear technology ... subject to the Atomic Energy Act and Nuclear Non‑Proliferation Act restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution actions are permitted so long as they do not introduce Munitions List items or restricted nuclear/atomic energy technology or otherwise change the invention's general nature triggering inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: License scope for applications required to be made available under 35 U.S.C. 181
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications or other materials that were required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181 will be eligible for a license of the scope provided in paragraph (b). Grant of this license authorizes the export of technical data pursuant to §5.11(b) and the filing of an application in a foreign country ... Further, this license includes the authority to export and file all duplicate and formal papers ... and to make amendments, modifications, and supplements to; file divisions of; and take any action in the prosecution of the foreign application, provided subject matter additional to that covered by the license is not involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files that were made available under 35 U.S.C. 181 receive a narrower license: they may be prosecuted abroad but cannot introduce subject matter beyond that already covered by the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing license scope and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition, accompanied by the required fee, may also be filed to change a license having the scope indicated in paragraph (b) of this section to a license having the scope indicated in paragraph (a). No such petition will be granted if the copy of the material filed pursuant to §5.13 or any corresponding United States application was required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may petition to broaden a license’s scope, but not if the materials were required to be made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181.

rubrics_metrics.name: No license required for prosecution actions not involving additional subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In those cases in which no license is required to file or export the foreign application, no license is required to file papers in connection with the prosecution of the foreign application not involving the disclosure of additional subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If initial foreign filing didn't require a license, routine prosecution papers that don't disclose new subject matter likewise do not require a separate license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers filed abroad that change general nature or disclose restricted subject matter must be separately licensed
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper filed abroad or transmitted to a foreign or international intellectual property authority following the filing of a foreign application that changes the general nature of the subject matter disclosed at the time of filing in a manner that would require such application to have been made available for inspection under 35 U.S.C. 181 or that involves the disclosure of subject matter listed in paragraph (a)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section must be separately licensed in the same manner as a foreign application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent foreign filings that materially change the application’s nature or disclose Munitions List or restricted nuclear information require a new license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining/dividing disclosures across separately granted licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses separately granted in connection with two or more United States applications may be exercised by combining or dividing the disclosures, as desired, provided: (1) Subject matter which changes the general nature ... or which involves subject matter listed in paragraph (a)(3)(i) or (ii) of this section is not introduced, and (2) In the case where at least one of the licenses was obtained under §5.12(b), additional subject matter is not introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may combine or divide disclosures from multiple licensed US applications abroad so long as no forbidden subject matter or new additional subject matter is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: License non-retroactivity and retroactive license petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A license does not apply to acts done before the license was granted. See §5.25 for petitions for retroactive licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have already filed or exported material before a license was granted, you must seek a retroactive license per §5.25; otherwise the license will not validate past acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with ITAR: arms, ammunition, and implements of war
rubrics_metrics.description: The exportation of technical data relating to arms, ammunition, and implements of war generally is subject to ITAR ... However, if a patent applicant complies with regulations issued by the Commissioner for Patents under 35 U.S.C. 184, no separate approval from the Department of State is required unless the applicant seeks to export technical data exceeding that used to support a patent application in a foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with Commissioner-issued regs can remove the need for separate Department of State approval for exports tied to patent filings, but only up to the level of technical data used to support the patent filing; exports exceeding that scope still need Department of State authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Munitions List subject matter is secret, no separate DoS request needed for modification petition
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent application containing subject matter on the Munitions List is subject to a secrecy order under §5.2 and a petition is made under §5.5 for a modification of the secrecy order to permit filing abroad, a separate request to the Department of State for authority to export classified information is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For secrecy‑ordered Munitions List subject matter, a §5.5 modification petition suffices without a separate DoS export authority request (per 22 CFR part 125).

rubrics_metrics.name: Export of technical data: filing in accordance with USPTO regs negates export license requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Department of Commerce regulations, a license is not required in any case to file a patent application or part thereof in a foreign country if the foreign filing is in accordance with the regulations (§§5.11 through 5.25) of the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complying with USPTO foreign-filing rules (§§5.11–5.25) means no separate Commerce export license is required for the filing itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export license exception for foreign-origin technical data sent to foreign inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: An export license is not required for data contained in a patent application prepared wholly from foreign-origin technical data where such application is being sent to the foreign inventor to be executed and returned to the United States for subsequent filing in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (15 CFR 734.10(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the application is entirely based on foreign-origin data and merely routed to the foreign inventor for execution and return, an export license under Commerce regs is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive nuclear technology treated as public for DOE regs when filed per USPTO regs
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed in accordance with the regulations (§§5.11 through 5.25) of the Patent and Trademark Office and eligible for foreign filing under 35 U.S.C. 184, is considered to be information available to the public in published form and a generally authorized activity for the purposes of the Department of Energy regulations (10 CFR 810.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you file in compliance with USPTO procedures and are eligible for foreign filing under 35 U.S.C. 184, DOE treats the application as publicly available for purposes of DOE export/assistance rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for retroactive license — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for retroactive license under 35 U.S.C. 184 shall be presented in accordance with §5.13 or §5.14(a), and shall include: (1) A listing of each of the foreign countries in which the unlicensed patent application material was filed; (2) The dates on which the material was filed in each country; (3) A verified statement (oath or declaration) containing: (i) An averment that the subject matter in question was not under a secrecy order at the time it was filed abroad, and that it is not currently under a secrecy order; (ii) A showing that the license has been diligently sought after discovery of the proscribed foreign filing; and (iii) An explanation of why the material was filed abroad through error without the required license ...; and (4) The required fee (§1.17(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A retroactive petition must list countries and dates, include a verified oath addressing secrecy status and efforts to obtain a license, explain the error with factual support, and include the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for retroactive license — evidentiary showing and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation ... must include a showing of facts rather than a mere allegation of action through error. The showing of facts ... should include statements by those persons having personal knowledge of the acts regarding filing in a foreign country and should be accompanied by copies of any necessary supporting documents such as letters of transmittal or instructions for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantiate claims of error with affidavits/declarations from witnesses with personal knowledge and supporting documentary evidence; describe acts covering the period up to and including each proscribed foreign filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive petition denial renewal period and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition for a retroactive license is denied, a time period of not less than thirty days shall be set, during which the petition may be renewed. Failure to renew ... will result in a final denial. A final denial stands unless a petition is filed under §1.181 within two months of the date of the denial. If the petition for a retroactive license is denied with respect to the invention of a pending application and no petition under §1.181 has been filed, a final rejection of the application under 35 U.S.C. 185 will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If denied, you get at least 30 days to renew; final denial may be appealed under §1.181 within two months, otherwise a pending application related to the denial may receive a final rejection under 35 U.S.C. 185.
